74: GEMARA: The reason is that he found, etc. - it is there [specifically] that it is said that the produce belongs to the owner of the vessel.

But [if he found a vessel] and produce was before it - then this produce belongs to the one who finds it, even though the vessel goes to the one who identifies the distinguishing mark. [The finder] must return the vessel, but he can retain the produce; we don't say that it must have fallen out of this vessel.

Some is in the vessel, etc. - the situation proves that those [fruits] on the ground belong to this other one, and [the finder] is required to return them to whomever furnishes the vessel's distinguishing mark; similarly regarding money [that must be returned] to the owner of the pouch.
